audit.why: 50.14% over 2505 games is a true even lane. Akshan owns levels 1-5 at 850 range; Sylas owns level 6 and the late game through Hijack.
audit.corrected: Difficulty stays 5.5/10 EVEN, but the level chart must show Sylas ahead at 6 and 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text credits the passive (Petricite Burst) with stealing ultimates.
audit.why: Hijack (R, 80/55/30s) steals ultimates. Petricite Burst is the on-attack chain proc. Sylas's spikes are level 6 (Hijack + Abduct pull) and his first AP item; Akshan's are level 3, level 6 Comeuppance, and first item swing-autos.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[1], whys[4] and mid to name Hijack.

audit.whatIsWrong: Abscond/Abduct described as a 'chain-stun'; foe want says he lands a 'root'.
audit.why: Sylas's E dash recasts into Abduct, a pull — not a stun or root. Chain Lash (Q, 10s at rank 1) slows. His only gap-closers are Abduct (13s rank 1) and Kingslayer (W, 400 range, heals off champions). Akshan's Avengerang out-ranges everything Sylas has at 850, and Heroic Swing (E) is knocked off on champion collision, so Abduct off a swing cancels it.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns block now states the 13s Abduct window and the anti-heal requirement against Kingslayer.

audit.why: Abduct at 13s rank 1 is the punish window; Hijack is 80s at rank 1.
Kingslayer heals off champion hits, so Grievous Wounds is genuinely needed here — already flagged in the report itemization line.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why contains garbled text ('Avengerang... no — R online') and calls Akshan's ultimate 'Vengeance'.

edits.before: Avengerang... no — R online: Vengeance executes the chipped from two screens. Chip, then channel.
edits.after: Both ultimates land: Comeuppance executes from two screens, but Hijack fires yours straight back.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Sylas wins by Abducting you off the wave, healing the trade back with Kingslayer, and casting your own Comeuppance at you once he hits 6.

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Heroic Swing for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Abduct is his only gap-closer and it is 13s at rank 1: once he dashes and whiffs the recast, step up for the next 13 seconds. - Kingslayer heals off you, so buy anti-heal before extended trades and hold E for his commit.

edits.before: Carry through strings and executes — chip everything, finish anything under a third, and let the swing write angles no one wards.
edits.after: Carry by never standing inside 400 units — Abduct's leash. Chip from 850 with Avengerang and Comeuppance whatever Kingslayer heals back.

edits.before: If Sylas gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Abscond / Abduct extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q strings and stay relevant through R executes.
edits.after: One kill and Kingslayer starts healing for real — farm outside 800 and never sit beside a wall he can Abduct you into. Two kills: refuse the trade entirely and chip toward Comeuppance range instead.

edits.before: Ahead, bully harder: string Sylas off every contact, swing-roam the rivers, and execute the map's mistakes with R.
edits.after: Ahead, deny his 6: shove first, roam so he farms alone, and Comeuppance him whenever Kingslayer leaves him short.

edits.before: Petricite Burst steals your ultimate for a free Comeuppance-style execute or repositioning tool, and his Q-E all-in becomes a real all-in threat the instant he's in range.
edits.after: Hijack steals your Comeuppance and fires that missing-health execute back at you, and with Abduct pulling him onto you his all-in is a real threat the instant he's in range.

edits.before: His stolen ultimate plus all-in combo suddenly makes him the bigger threat in a fight.
edits.after: Hijack takes your Comeuppance, and Abduct's pull makes him the bigger threat in a fight.

edits.before: All-in immediately with Q-E after landing his root
edits.after: All-in with Chain Lash's slow, then Abduct you into W

edits.before: The moment he hits 6, everything flips: Petricite Burst can hijack your own Comeuppance or another priority ultimate on the enemy team, and paired with Q-E his all-in becomes genuinely threatening, so you have to respect his kill pressure in this window and around 11.
edits.after: The moment he hits 6, everything flips: Hijack can steal your own Comeuppance or another priority ultimate on the enemy team, and paired with Abduct's pull his all-in becomes genuinely threatening, so you have to respect his kill pressure in this window and around 11.
